newsitem.title: JAPAN: Deng death no effect on Japan-Sino relations.
newsitem.headline: Deng death no effect on Japan-Sino relations.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday he was saddened by the death of Deng Xiaoping, and foreign ministry officials were quoted as saying there would not be no major effect on Sino-Japanese relations.
In a prepared statement, Hashimoto said: "I am filled with great sadness on hearing the news of Deng Xiaoping's death."

"The importance of the Japan-China relationship is of growing importance for peace and stability in Asia and the world. I will continue to work with China's leaders for the long-term stability of our bilateral relationship," he said.

NHK Television quoted Foreign Ministry officials as saying Japan did not expect major political or economic change within China since the current political structure centred on President Jiang Zemin was stable and economic reforms were under way.

But they said the Japanese government would keep a close eye on developments in China. They cited the growing gap between the rich in cities and the poor in the country, the apparent growth in power of the military after tensions with Taiwan, and nuclear testing by the Chinese government.
